newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Sfr, yen dominate modest Hungary FX futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Sfr, yen dominate modest Hungary FX futures trade.

text.p: The Swiss franc and yen continued to feature strongly on the futures market of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Tuesday while no deals were struck on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE), traders said.
The BCE's financial section posted modest turnover of 3.995 billion forints.
Dealers believe the Swiss franc and the yen, with their low interest rates, represent a good tool with which to speculate on the crawling peg devalution of the forint.
From April the rate will be reduced to 1.1 percent per month from 1.2 percent.
Swiss franc futures were unchanged at 136.80 for December, which accounted for most turnover in the Swiss unit.
Trade in the yen was shared between September, which rose 90 fillers to 157.55 forints per 100 yen, and December, which rose 54 fillers to 163.54.
Tuesday's central bank midday fix for the two currencies was 121.30 forints for the Swiss franc and 143.61 forints per 100 yen.
A tradeless BSE futures market saw no price changes.
